round: the tester's two findings, worked as the architect scoped them: two rules, each removing a class, and nothing else

proof.criterion: The tester's first finding — a numeric knob too large for the shell broke both of the script's promises: `LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=9223372036854775808` exited 2 with dash's `Illegal number` (the one outcome the header says it cannot produce, which stops the role's agent), and `LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_HOLD=99999999999999999999` left the run holding the cache's lock past every bound.
proof.surface: The real script run by hand in a scratch workspace on this volume, and a throwaway copy of this tree with a hanging install and a `flock` contender; plus the script's 260-assertion suite, which carries the tester's own red cases.
proof.command: env LEGION_WORKSPACE=<scratch> LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=9223372036854775807|9223372036854775808|99999999999999999999|270|08 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; then env … LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=3 LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_HOLD=99999999999999999999 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh against a hanging install, timed ; bash scripts/legion-setup.test.sh
proof.observed: `9223372036854775808` and `99999999999999999999` now exit 0 with the default in force and the sentence in the report; `9223372036854775807`, the largest this shell can use, is still taken and runs the install; `08` is refused as before. The hold the tester measured still running at 25 s ends in **4 s measured** against a 3 s budget: `install-timeout`/124, the refusal at the head of its detail, no marker, and `/usr/bin/flock -w 2` takes the cache immediately afterwards. The suite reports `Results: 260 passed, 0 failed`, the tester's red cases among them and unmodified.
proof.negativeControl: The rule is the class, not the two values: a value reaches neither `$((…))` nor `[ … -le … ]` unless its text is a digit string this shell can work with — length first, then an equal-length string comparison against the largest it takes, so nothing unvalidated is ever compared numerically. That is what makes the hold's failure mode unreachable rather than handled: `[ 5 -le 99999999999999999999 ]` is itself an `Illegal number`, and its non-zero status took the `|| left=$hold` branch, which is how `timeout -k 5 <huge>` came to bound nothing.

proof.criterion: The tester's second finding — the exemption marker must be a comment's business, and text that is not a shell comment bought a pass for a vulnerable command on the same line whenever the line's quotes did not balance.
proof.surface: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh against fixtures built as its own suite builds them, and its 179-case suite.
proof.command: a fixture whose scripts/probe.sh holds `echo "see # check-check-commands: allow docs && bunx biome check .`, its single-quote twin, the balanced version of the same line, `echo don't # check-check-commands: allow …` and a balanced line carrying a genuine trailing marker ; then PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh and .test.sh over the real tree
proof.observed: Both unbalanced lines are reported, as is the balanced one whose marker sits inside a string (round 2's case, still green). The line that names no pinned tool is still no problem of this gate's, and a balanced line's genuine trailing marker still exempts it — the marker remains a comment's business where there is a comment. The tree passes with 13 manifests, 8 workflows, 92 shell scripts and 551 guides, and the suite reports `Results: 179 passed, 0 failed`.
proof.negativeControl: The rule is one reading, not two quote characters: where the scan that judges the command says the text after a `#` is inside an unterminated quote, there is no comment there and therefore no marker — which is what `judge`'s own docstring already claimed. The second scan that tracked the other quote character is gone, so no spelling of the same trick survives it.

proof.criterion: The repository's own checks at this head, since the install half changed again.
proof.surface: A throwaway copy of this tree on the issue volume with the packages installed by the script itself.
proof.command: sh scripts/legion-setup.sh ; ./node_modules/.bin/biome --version ; bun run typecheck and bun test in packages/pi-legion ; bun run lint . at the root
proof.observed: The install exits 0, biome is `Version: 2.4.11`, typecheck is clean, `bun test` is 531 tests and 0 failed, and the whole-tree Biome run is `Checked 1079 files`, exit 0.
proof.negativeControl: In this issue's own workspace, which has no node_modules, `bun run lint packages/pi-legion/` and `bun run typecheck` still exit 1 with the wrapper's message while `bunx biome check .` exits 0 answering 0.3.3 — AC1's state, left as the tester needs it.

filesChanged: scripts/legion-setup.sh: `use_seconds` refuses a digit string this shell cannot work with, by its text alone, before any arithmetic or comparison touches it.
.github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh: `split_comment` returns no comment for a line whose quotes do not balance, so the exemption comes from the reading that judges the command.
trickyParts: The boundary is the shell's integer range rather than a shape, so the check is a length and then an equal-length string comparison — `9223372036854775807` is taken, `9223372036854775808` is not, and neither is ever handed to arithmetic.

A value just under the range wraps rather than failing (`$((1 + 9223372036854775807))` is negative), which for the budget means a deadline in the past; `remaining()`'s floor of 1 keeps that harmless, and the tester's observation of it is why the two edges are documented separately.
deviations: Nothing else was touched this round, on the architect's instruction: no tidying, no fast-follow, no retro note, so that if this work is split the install half is refiled with a clean record of what it has and has not got.
openQuestions: The architect has put the continuation to a human (dispatch://INFRA-71/ask/d34a1f9c-2b33-4b5e-a131-cd760f0a0437): one more round then stop, ship with both holes written down, or split the check half from the install script. This head is the two rules it asked for under two of those three answers.
